summary: Embedded dashboard auto-refresh causes tracehook redirects to org root and drops trace parameters
description:
Issue summary: PilotDocs reports that when their product embeds a Redwood dashboard panel (iframe) with the panel auto-refresh enabled, tracehook links generated by the widget intermittently redirect to the customer's org root (/org/<org-id>/console) instead of preserving the trace anchor parameters (trace_id, start_ts). Impact: opening a trace link from an embedded panel often results in a missing trace context or a 404; users see the console but without the expected trace or timeline.

Impact: Customer-facing debugging workflows are interrupted; PilotDocs engineers cannot jump from an alert or dashboard row to the specific trace (high frequency during their morning dashboards). Several teams reported inability to investigate incidents originating from PilotDocs' embedded dashboards which is blocking release.

Environment: Production (us-east) — PilotDocs uses an iframe embed with our standard embed token + auto-refresh interval of 30s. Occurs across Chrome and Safari. Affects only embedded views; native console links open correctly.

Observed since: 2026-03-09 09:00 UTC. Volume: PilotDocs reports ~12% of tracehook clicks from embeds failing; our internal analytics show a matching jump in 302/redirect responses for the embed-proxy service for their org.

Expected behavior: Tracehook links opened from embedded panels should forward to the console with the full trace anchor preserved, opening the trace view (console/trace/<trace_id>) and maintaining time bounds.

Actual behavior: Users are redirected to org root or to an auth landing page where trace parameters are stripped or not processed, requiring manual search.

Additional notes: PilotDocs upgraded to the embed SDK v2.1.1 last week; they also rotated an embed token on 2026-03-08 which may be correlated.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer embeds a Redwood dashboard panel in an iframe with auto-refresh enabled (interval 30s)
Open the embedded page in a fresh browser session (incognito reproducible)
Trigger a dashboard row drilldown that generates a tracehook link (click trace link icon)
Observe the navigation target: sometimes lands on /org/<org-id>/console (no trace loaded) or an auth prompt; expected: console/trace/<trace-id> with trace loaded
Repeat until failure manifests (in customer cases ~1 in 8 clicks)
logs: 2026-03-09T09:14:21Z console[pid=1102] WARN missing query params: trace_id not found for request /org/abc123/console
2026-03-09T09:14:22Z auth[pid=900] DEBUG token_lookup: embed_token=rotated-2026-03-08 (PilotDocs) matched, session cookie not present
comments: 2026-03-10 — Asha Narayanan (Support): Opened with initial reproduce steps and customer-provided HAR. Noted that native console links are fine; problem isolated to embeds.

2026-03-10 — Ethan Brooks (SRE): Took ownership for investigation. Initial hypothesis: embed-proxy redirect flow may be dropping fragment params (#trace=) when using 302 vs 307 semantics. Adding tracing on proxy to confirm.

2026-03-11 — PilotDocs (Customer via CS): We see the issue on users in EMEA as well but much less frequent; happy to provide a short-screen recording of failing clicks and the embed configuration. We rotated tokens last Tuesday and upgraded SDK on Thursday.

2026-03-11 — Ethan Brooks (SRE): Correlated metrics — embed-proxy 302 rate for PilotDocs increased after token rotation. Reproduced locally when embed SDK triggers a redirect path that constructs link with fragment (hash) instead of query param; hash is lost across server-side redirects.

2026-03-12 — Product (Nora Li): Noted a recent change in embed SDK v2.1.1 that changed redirect type; assigned to frontend team to review. Creating follow-up engineering ticket for SDK fix and server-side fallback.
investigation_notes: Checked embed-proxy codepath: when we receive /embed/redirect with fragment-only anchor (#trace=...), current code issues a 302 to /org/<org>/console (fragment not forwarded by browsers on 302).
Reproduced locally by constructing redirect with fragment in Location header — confirmed browsers drop fragment on 302. 307 preserves fragment in some cases but not reliable across proxies.
PilotDocs embed SDK v2.1.1 constructs links with fragment instead of query param due to a change in SDK anchor construction (commit 9f3b2a1).

Temporary mitigation considered: rewrite embed-proxy to convert fragment into query parameter server-side and issue direct 200 with meta refresh or an HTML page that executes a client-side redirect preserving fragment.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided to customer: change embed SDK to build trace links using query params (trace_id=<id>&start_ts=<ts>) instead of fragment, or disable auto-refresh until fix is released.

Short-term fix (in progress): update embed-proxy to return an HTML relay page (200) that does client-side window.location = targetWithHash so browser preserves fragment — patch in review (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4567).

Long-term fix: revert SDK behavior to construct trace links as query params OR update proxy to consistently translate fragments to query params and use 307/HTML relay as appropriate. Frontend and SDK teams assigned; target patch release 2026-03-18.

Follow-ups: Add an automated test in embed-sdk that verifies redirect semantics across common browsers; schedule runbook update describing embed token rotation impact and how to validate tracehooks post-rotation.
